sections.evaluation_comments:
8/13/2026
During AM kennel cleaning, animal care staff radioed for assistance moving dog over to clean kennel. Worker reported that the dog would growl, lunge at kennel front, with tense body, showing teeth. When leadership went to support, dog was already on the side of the kennel that they needed to be on but due to behavior, unable to close portal door. Leadership approached dog with hotdog and dog nicely took hotdog out of handlers hand. Handler again presented a hotdog and dog took hotdog nicely out of hand. Handler asked animal care staff to try and distract dog with the hotdogs so handler would be able to reach inside neighboring kennel to close portal door. Animal care employee presented hotdog and dog nicely took hotdog out of hand once more and did not notice handler's attempt to close portal door and was able to successfully close it with no issues as dog was distracted by worker presenting hotdog. However, when handler went to place lock through lock hole to secure the kennel, dog started to bark and lung to front of kennel door at handler with tense body, wide eyes, and showing teeth. Handler and worker disengaged with the dog and kennel and dog stopped barking and retreated in the back of kennel.
8/9/2026
Dog was standing in middle of kennel with an intense posture, weight shifted evenly, curling lips, growling & ears pinned back.  Handler would kennel flirt with dog while offering treats, would approach handler for treats after a few moments & started to relax body.  Opened kennel door & presented leash.  Dog would lunge forward while growling with ears pinned back again & whale eyed, handler removed leash.  Closed door & offered more treats.  Presented leash again, dog would lunge again while catching leash in mouth, biting & pulling back on leash.  Once dropped, handler would attempt to leash again, dog would keep lunging forward while biting & pulling leash.  On 4th attempt, dog would air snap towards handlers gloved hands after dropping leash from mouth, not making contact then would start to dilate pupils while standing with body weight evenly distributed, ears pinned back & growling loudly.  Due to high FAS & safety concerns, handler ended attempt to leash dog.
8/8/2026
Dog was at front of kennel, tense body. Sniffed towards hand when presented, then began low growling. Handler spoke softly, tried coaxing. Dog growled louder, alarm barked, lunged against gate. Handler shook treat bag, dog stopped growling, ears perked, watched bag. Eagerly ate treats tossed into kennel. Handler gave several treats, cracked gate open, neutrally presented leash. Dog became wide-eyed, pupils dilated, intense growling. Stared at leash, then handler. Dog would snarl, whip head, bite towards leash when handler attempted to place it. Repeated this several times. Handler would close gate, dog settled, came forward to accept treats, resumed reactivity when leash was presented in kennel. Handler cast leash, dog did not react to contact, handler gave praise and treats, repeated this a few times, then was able to drape leash w/ large loop. Dog was tense on leash, accepted more treats. Handler used large behavior tote, secured it over dog. Dog snarled, moved erratically under tote, lunged against it. Second handler arrived, assisted securing top of tote. Dog continued to snarl, lunge against it, attempting to bite through tote walls. Handlers removed tote from kennel, carried to M&G room. Removed tote lid. Dog looked around, tense. Leash had slipped off, handler was able to slowly place second slip lead without issue. Tilted tote, dog hopped out. Handler kept hold of leash. Dog sniffed around room, approached second handler, accepted treats by hand, mouthy. Allowed some gentle petting, slight flinch, moved away. Continued walking around room. Approached for more treats. Relieved self. Second handler brought thick blanket into room, placed it on floor briefly, dog approached, began rolling on blanket, allowed more petting. Second handler was able to pick dog up with blanket, leaving face exposed. Trembled while being carried, removed leash by hand, returned to kennel. Handler left treat jackpot before exiting.
8/5/2026
walks on leash, allows some handling and petting, advanced restraint for vaccines, trembling, reactive to being picked up, grumbling on approach, pancaking, per ASO dog is food reactive w/ possible resource guarding

8/18/2026
Dog jumped and placed front paws onto kennel door, soliciting attention from handler when handler came to move dog. Dog took hot dog treats gently. Easy to leash and pull from kennel, did not engage with other dogs while moving through kennel building. Dog walked slowly alongside handler, jumping on handlers legs occasionally, soliciting attention. On the walk to new building, dog pancaked, laying on the sidewalk, when dogs started barking loudly, but after dogs stopped barking, dog started moving again. While handler was putting on PPE, dog sat on handlers feet, leaning against handler. Dog walked right into new kennel, and allowed to be unleash by hand.

Solicited attentions, Easy to pull from kennel, Easy to return to kennel, Not interested in toys, Takes treats nicely, Easy/Loose Leash, Calm, Ignored dogs when walking past kennels, Affectionate, friendly, loves attention, stayed close to handler in yard, gentle, displayed nice manners, soft eyes, good boy.

Solicited attentions, Difficult to pull from kennel, Easy to return to kennel, Not interested in toys, Takes treats nicely, Carried, Calm, Timid, Ignored dogs when walking past kennels, Sit, Shake, had to taxi to and from play yard. let me pick him up and put him in taxi. once in the yard, he opened up and was very affectionate. gave kisses and allowed petting all over. leaned in for pets.
7/19/2026
Dog was at front of kennel, soft face, wiggly body, panting. Put front feet on gate, accepted treats. Easy to leash, exited kennel slowly. Dog walked to building door, then froze once it was open, appearing nervous. Handler crouched, coaxed dog gently, dog crawled forward to handler. Once outside, dog walked loose leash, body low at times, close to handler. Handler stopped to wait for a staff member to pass ahead, this dog gently jumped up and rested front feet on handler, making eye contact with soft face. Handler petted dog, encouraged on. No issues on way to yard. In main play yard, dog was affiliative with handler and sought attention, allowed all petting. Jumped up a few times to lean in. Accepted treats gently. Appeared nervous of loud outside surroundings, but did begin exploring independently after a few minutes. Greeted another staff member over fence, allowed them to pet and give treats. Loose leash walk on return, dog frequently looking up at handler. Entered kennel with light direction, allowed leash removal by hand.
*Dog should not be introduced to any other pets until end of 14-day decompression period. Potential adopters should be counseled on proper dog introductions, which must be slow and supervised. This approach is essential for the safety, comfort, and well-being of all pets involved.*
7/16/2026
Able to leash, dog walking stop n go , planting butt at Triage door. Able to lift in room. In room, dog would loosen body, then tense again. Took treast from handler. Able to restrain for vaccines. Lifted into bucket and rode to kennel with no issue. Used clip leash for leash removal

08/18/26 12:01 This dog is experiencing significant stress and anxiety in the shelter, particularly while kenneled. These behaviors are often a response to the overwhelming sights, sounds, and confinement, along with the lack of choice or control over their environment. Although this dog continues to show appropriate behavior outside of the kennel with positive interactions with staff and volunteers,without intervention, well-being will continue to decline. Immediate placement is needed with an experienced adopter or New Hope Partner who can provide time and space to decompress in a calm, supportive home. Placement needed by close of business 8/23/26. May be at risk of euthanasia 8/24/26 or sooner if warranted.

Handler approached outside gate due to cleaning; dog was at gate, rhythmic demand barking, jumping up against kennel. Handler used treats, verbal coaxing to direct dog down. In yard, dog had high energy, explored surroundings, came to handler when called and leaned in for petting. Allowed all petting and handling. Demonstrated "sit" and "paw" commands, took treats eagerly but gently. Very interested in toys, chased them when thrown, laid at handler's feet while playing. Dog continued to explore, rolled around in mud puddle, returned to handler and began settling, seeking attention. No issues on return. Dog appeared alert to dog in neighboring yard, ears perked, but did not attempt to engage. Entered kennel with light direction, allowed leash removal by hand.
